- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, model frequently underestimates downside; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 3–5 days of forecast) — especially when sentiment is volatile — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 3 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is near recent mean, model often overfits to recent highs; apply a 1–2% mean-reversion correction toward 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows a clear downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it — apply a 1–3% downward bias to the latter half of forecast.
